ORAL ORDER 5 07-08-2025 Heard the learned counsel for the appellants as well as the learned APP for the State.

2. This appeal has been preferred against the Judgment and sentence dated 11.6.2024 and 21.6.2024 passed by Additional Sessions Judge -III Nalanda at Bihar sharif in Sessions Trial no. 511/2014 Tulsi Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66077651/

sentences.text: 1 where by where under Applicant Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.3349 of 2024(5) dt.07-08-2025 has convicted and sentenced U/s 354(B)/34 of I. P.C under go R.1 for five years and a fine of Rs 5000/- and in default of payment of fine further undergo S. I for 3 months, u/s 323/34 of I.P.C under go S.I for one year and fine of Rs 1000/- and in default of payment of fine further undergo S.I for 1 month.
And u/s 341/34 of I.P.C under go S.I for one month and fine of Rs 500/- in default of payment of fine further undergo S.I for 10 days.
All the sentences shall concurrently.
3. According to the FIR, appellant Ravi Kumar wrapped towel around the neck of the victim and pulled her with bad intention.
The appellant Tulsi Kumar was also present there.
Both the appellants attempted to commit rape.
They snatched a golden chain from the victim.

4. While making the prayer for bail and suspension of sentence, learned counsel for the appellants has submitted that the attempt to commit rape was not found true and even the charges have not been framed under Section 376/511 of the IPC.
The appellants have been convicted under Section 323/34, 341/34, and 324(B)/34 of the IPC.
The maximum punishment awarded to the appellants is 5 years R.I.
The Appellant Ravi Kumar has suffered incarceration of 1 year and 9 months, whereas the appellant Tulsi Kumar has suffered incarceration Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.3349 of 2024(5) dt.07-08-2025 for 1 year and 7 months.
5. On the other hand, the learned APP for the State has opposed the prayer for bail and suspension of sentence.

6. Considering the above-mentioned facts and circumstances as well as the fact that there is no likelihood of the appeal being taken up for hearing in near future, this Court accepts the prayer for bail of the appellants.

Accordingly, let the appellants above-named be enlarged on bail during the pendency of this appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Ten Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Sessions Judge -III Nalanda at Bihar sharif in Sessions Trial no. 511/2014.
7. The execution of sentence shall remain suspended during the pendency of this appeal.
